panels.title: Upload vs Download over Time
panels.description: Bytes per interval in each direction. 'Upload' is src → dst as the flow was first seen, so for a flow initiated from outside, upload is inbound. Needs fields added by the collector upgrade, so it stays empty for any part of the range recorded before that.

panels.title: Upload / Download Split
panels.description: Total bytes each way over the range.

panels.title: Upload Share
panels.description: Upload as a percentage of all bytes. A normally-browsing network sits well below 50%; a sustained climb means this network is sending more than it receives, which is worth explaining.

panels.title: Upload vs Download by Host
panels.description: Per source host. A high upload share on a host that should mostly consume data is the asymmetry worth chasing.

panels.title: Top Uploads to Public Destinations
panels.description: Bytes sent from any host to a public (non-RFC1918) address, largest first. This is the data-egress view: a host near the top that has no business sending bulk data outward is the finding.

panels.title: Upload vs Download by Service
panels.description: Direction split per destination service. Services that should be download-dominated (http/https) showing heavy upload deserve a look.

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict every panel to traffic with either endpoint in this range, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16, 10.12.6.0/24, or a bare IP. Leave empty for no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary, so /20 behaves as /16 and may show a wider range than typed.
